doc.title: feat(drive): randomizeRange for drive sheets (#1830)
doc.body:
Split out of #1830. Blocker #1831 closed as [ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md).

## What

`randomizeRange` has no request type in `src/drive/sheets/`. Shuffles the row
order within a range randomly (server-side; the resulting order is not
caller-specified or predictable).

Proposed verb: `randomize-range` (15 chars).

## Gate — resolved

[ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md)
§3 initially placed `randomizeRange` under `sheets-write` alone, on a
values-only reading, but flagged (§5) that whether the server carries a
row's **formatting** along with it when reordering was an open question with
a pre-decided consequence: if verified true, the gate becomes the
**`sheets-write` + `sheets-structure` union**.

Live-verified 2026-09-22 against a probe sheet in `omni-dev-test`
(`sortRange` and `randomizeRange` both tested; findings below apply to
this issue's `randomizeRange`):

- **Formatting moves with the row** — the §5 trigger fires. Gate is the
  union of `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure`
  (`target_gate::resolve_all`, the shape `text-to-columns` took in #1867).
- **Notes and data-validation rules move with the row** too.
- **In-range formulas move with their row and have their relative
  references rewritten**, so each formula keeps pointing at its own row.
- **Cells in the same rows but outside the selected columns do not
  move** — confirms §3's record-decoupling caveat: a range narrower than
  its rows can silently detach a record's other columns.

(The already-merged `sort-range` (#1842) predates this measurement and
shipped under `sheets-write` alone; a fix-forward for it is filed as
#1870, out of scope for this issue.)

## `--dry-run`

Cannot preview the resulting order (server-side randomness, same class of
limitation `autoFill` has for different reasons). Reports the range being
reordered, states plainly that the current row order is not preserved, and
leads with the range-width-vs-sheet-width record-integrity caveat before
the smaller "references outside the range may see a different row's
value" caveat — never a cell's contents.

## Status

Plan and live-verification findings posted in comments below. Branch
`issue-1845-randomize-range`, rebased even with `main`. Implementation not
yet started.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Plan

State of play: the blocker #1831 closed as [ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md) (numbered 0083, not the 0082 predicted in #1831's own plan comment). Sort-range (#1842, PR #1866), auto-fill (#1840, PR #1862) and text-to-columns (#1843, PR #1867) are all merged, and sort-range is the near-exact template for this verb. This worktree currently sits 12 commits behind `main` and predates sort-range, so step 1 rebases before anything else. No other grid-mutation PR is open right now, so the tracker's two-at-a-time snapshot-collision rule isn't a live constraint.

### What ADR-0083 fixes for this verb
- **§3**: `randomizeRange` joins `sheets-write` alone, on the values-only reading — a permutation of the range's own cells is a strict special case of what a `sheets-write` grant already permits via `clear`+`write`.
- **§6, "nothing discarded" tier**: no `values` read in `--dry-run`. The preview names the range, leads with the range-width-vs-sheet's-allocated-width record-integrity caveat (a narrower selection can silently decouple a record's other columns), then the smaller "references outside the range may see a different row's value" caveat. Never a value, and never a claim of predicting the resulting order — it's server-side randomness.
- **§5**: `randomizeRange` (alongside `sortRange`) is explicitly named as a live-verification item for two open questions: whether the server carries a row's **formatting** with it when moved, and what happens to a **formula inside the range** (moved with its row, references rewritten or not, or left in place). If formatting moves, the ADR's fixed rule requires flipping the gate to **both** `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure` (the text-to-columns precedent, which hit exactly this). Sort-range shipped *without* doing this verification, so this issue is the first time it actually gets answered for the reorder pair — and if the answer is "yes, formatting moves," sort-range's gate needs the same fix as a follow-up.

### Steps

1. **Rebase onto `origin/main`** so `src/drive/sheets/sort_range.rs` and its CLI module are present to mirror.
2. **Wire type** in `src/drive/sheets/types.rs`: `RandomizeRangeRequest { range: GridRange }` plus a `BatchUpdateRequestItem::RandomizeRange` variant, doc comment citing ADR-0083 §3, and a serialization test asserting `{"randomizeRange":{"range":{...}}}`.
3. **Engine** `src/drive/sheets/randomize_range.rs` — a trimmed copy of `sort_range.rs` with the sort-spec machinery removed. Same options struct minus `sort_by`; same result shape (`WouldChange`/`Changed` carrying `range` + `width_warning`); same flow: A1 compose → `target_gate::resolve` on `SheetsWrite` → `spreadsheets.get` → bounded-range refusal → width warning → dry-run returns before any lease/batchUpdate → `LeasedWrite` + `conclude_native_leased_write` for the real run. Log operation `sheets-randomize-range`. Lift the `width_warning` helper out of `sort_range.rs` into a shared `grid_range` helper rather than duplicating it (mirrors how #1843 lifted `non_blank_locations`).
4. **Preview/output wording**: dry-run — "Would randomize the row order of {range} in {book}" plus "the resulting order is chosen by the server and cannot be previewed; the current row order will not be preserved." Real run — "Randomized the row order of {range}" plus the outside-references caveat. No cell contents ever.
5. **CLI** `src/cli/drive/sheets/randomize_range.rs`: `randomize-range <ID> --range <A1> [--sheet NAME] [--dry-run] [lease flag] [-o]`. Register `RandomizeRange` in `SheetsSubcommands` right after `SortRange`, `pub mod` in `src/drive/sheets.rs`. Verb name is 15 chars, well inside the 27-char cap.
6. **Live verification (ADR-0083 §5)** — the step sort-range skipped. Back up `~/.omni-dev/settings.json`, add a temporary `sheets-write`-only rule scoped to the `omni-dev-test` folder, build a sheet with a bold/coloured row and a relative formula inside the target range, randomize it, read back values/formatting, restore settings and md5-verify. Record both findings in `docs/drive.md`:
   - If formatting moves with rows → switch the gate to `target_gate::resolve_all` over both operations, update the `SheetsStructure` doc comment, and file a follow-up issue for sort-range (same defect, different verb).
   - Formula-movement finding → caveat wording only, doesn't move the gate.
7. **Docs/sync**: new `#### drive sheets randomize-range` section in `docs/drive.md` between sort-range and auto-fill; add the verb to the default-policy table's `sheets-write` row; extend `SheetsWrite`'s doc comment in `src/drive/write_gate.rs`; `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry citing #1845 and ADR-0083 §§3, 5, 6.
8. **Tests**, mirroring sort-range's set: request JSON, CLI parse, dry-run makes no `values` read and no batchUpdate, real run sends one `randomizeRange` request, open-ended/unknown-sheet refusals, denied-gate attempt recording, all four lease refusals, every `describe_lines` arm, jsonl output. Then the `update-snapshots` skill for the help golden, and a local `cargo llvm-cov --lib` pass before trusting any posted PR coverage comment.
9. **Ship**: commit as `feat(drive): add sheets randomize-range command`, lint with `omni-dev git commit message lint origin/main..HEAD`, open a PR fixing #1845 citing ADR-0083 §§3, 5, 6, then tick the tracker checkbox in #1830.

### Calls made without asking
- Require a fully bounded range, same as sort-range (`A2:D100`, not `A:A`/`2:2`).
- No confirmation flag (ADR-0075 §3), consistent with the rest of the tranche.

### Flagged for visibility
If step 6's live verification finds that formatting moves with reordered rows, the scope grows beyond this issue alone: it changes this verb's gate to a two-operation composition *and* surfaces that sort-range (#1842, already merged) is mis-gated under the same rule, requiring a follow-up there. That's in-scope per ADR-0083 §5's own fixed rule, not a scope decision I'm making unilaterally.

comments.body:
## Residual resolved — live verification run before implementing

The plan above left one fork open (step 6: ADR-0083 §5's formatting/formula question). It has now been measured live rather than deferred to implementation time, by sending the real `sortRange` and `randomizeRange` requests to a probe sheet (`omni-dev #1845 reorder probe` in `omni-dev-test`, left in place) and reading the grid back with `includeGridData`.

Probe layout: A2:C6 with one bold+pink row, one row carrying a note, one cell with a data-validation rule, a relative formula per row in column C, plus an absolute and a relative reference in column D (same rows, outside the reordered columns) and a `=B2` reference from row 7 outside the range.

**Findings, identical for both requests:**

- **Formatting moves with the row.** That is §5's pre-decided trigger, so `randomize-range` gates on **both `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure`** (`target_gate::resolve_all`, the shape `text-to-columns` took in #1867). Not a fork any more.
- **Notes and data-validation rules move with the row** as well.
- **In-range formulas move with their row and their relative references are rewritten** (`=B3*2` became `=B2*2` once its row landed on row 2), so each formula keeps pointing at its own row. This fixes §6's caveat wording: the risk is not formulas *inside* the range, it is references *into* it from outside.
- **Cells in the same rows but outside the selected columns stay put** and now read a different record's value — §3's record-decoupling caveat, confirmed, and the reason the preview leads with the width warning.
- `randomizeRange` returns an empty reply; the real run reports what it sent.

**Plan amendments:**

- Step 3/6: gate is the two-operation union from the first commit; no conditional branch. `docs/drive.md`'s section records all four facts, and the `SheetsStructure` doc comment gains `randomize-range`.
- Step 7: the default-policy table lists `randomize-range` under both `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure` (as `text-to-columns` is), not under `sheets-write` alone.
- Step 8: add the union-gate test — a rule allowing `sheets-write` but explicitly denying `sheets-structure` yields `Blocked`.
- Sort-range is mis-gated by the same rule; filed as #1870 rather than widening this issue.

The routing signal's "design needs opus (close call)" was pointing at exactly this open fork. With it measured, what remains is implementation on a settled design.

doc.title: feat(jev): sharpen route's complexity-reduction signal (could_be_cheaper scope, citation relations, tier margins, spike detection)
doc.body:
## Summary

Four related gaps in `omni-dev ai jev route`'s ability to tell a reader *why* an issue
classified the way it did and *what would lower it*, found by using `route` against
issue #1845 during that issue's own triage (2026-09-22 — see that issue's comment
thread for the worked example this issue is built from):

1. **`could_be_cheaper` is design-stage only**, so it gives no signal when `implement`
   is the higher stage (`class = max(design, implement)`).
2. **Citation detection can't distinguish a real dependency from provenance.** `find_citations`
   treats "Blocked on #N" and "Split out of #N" identically, so a `could_be_cheaper`
   question gets asked about a parent tracker whose closure was never actually a
   precondition for the routed issue's own work.
3. **Text output hides the runner-up tier.** `Answer::Choice` already carries a full
   `probabilities` map; `render_stage_line`/`render_stage_clause` render only the
   winning choice and its confidence, so "close call" gives no sense of what it was
   close *to* without switching to `-o json`.
4. **No way to distinguish "needs judgment" from "needs a spike."** The `stage_design`
   question asks whether "the text already settles the approach and the open
   questions" — but an "open question" can mean two very different things: genuine
   unresolved judgment (needs a higher-tier model to think it through), or a single
   bounded, already-specified empirical test whose result mechanically selects between
   two already-decided branches (a spike). `route` currently scores both the same way.

## Motivation — the #1845 case

#1845 (`randomizeRange` for `drive sheets`) was routed while its design was gated on
one live-verification question from [ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md)
§5: does the Sheets API carry a row's formatting along with it when reordering? The
ADR had *already* pre-decided the consequence either way — if yes, gate on both
`sheets-write` and `sheets-structure`; if no, `sheets-write` alone — so the only
remaining work was running the test and applying the rule its answer selected. No
further architectural judgment was needed.

`route` classified `design` as `opus`, confidence 0.18, "close call" — reasonable
given what it could see (item 4: the issue's own text, and the ADR it linked to but
`build_route_state` deliberately excludes for token cost, read as an unresolved open
question with no way to tell it apart from a genuinely hard one), but not actually
telling the operator "the way to lower this is to spend 20 minutes on one bounded API
probe," which is what running it actually was. The `depends_on` line the same run
produced (`cites open #1830, which could leave less design work if resolved (0.43)`)
pointed at the tracker issue #1845 was split out of, which was never itself a
precondition for closing this issue's design fork — items 1 and 2 above.

## Proposed changes

### 1. Extend `could_be_cheaper` to the `implement` stage

Same mechanism #1812 shipped for `design` (`could_be_cheaper_question` in
`src/jev/route.rs`), asked a second time per open citation, keyed
`could_be_cheaper.implement` in the report. #1812's own Open Questions section already
flagged this as deferred, not abandoned, for exactly this reason (rust-works/succinctly#2063 in that
issue's evidence was a citation whose real bearing was on `implement`, untested at the
time). Needs the same live-evidence validation round #1812 ran for `design` before the
wording ships — not done as part of this issue.

### 2. Relation-aware citation weighting

Recognize "blocked on"/"blocks"/"depends on"/"requires" phrasing near a citation as a
stronger dependency signal than a bare `#N` or "split from"/"tracker"/"split out of"
phrasing, and either suppress `could_be_cheaper` for the weak-signal case or label it
distinctly in the report (`relation: "tracker"` vs `relation: "blocker"`) so a reader
can discount it themselves. The cheaper version of this — labeling rather than
suppressing — avoids guessing wrong and hiding a real dependency; suppressing outright
is riskier and would need its own evidence round given #1812's Round 1 finding that
even Jev-driven signals here get fooled by how the citing sentence is actually worded.

### 3. Show the runner-up tier in text output

`render_stage_clause`/`render_stage_line` (`src/jev/route.rs`) already have
`answer.probabilities` on hand (`Answer::Choice`'s full distribution from Jev); add
the second-highest tier and its probability to the close-call case only, e.g.
`opus (0.18, close call — sonnet 0.16)`. Pure rendering change, no new Jev call, no
wording to validate — lowest-cost item here and shippable without an evidence round.

### 4. A spike-vs-judgment signal

The most novel and least validated item. Proposed as a new `noul` question per
routed issue (not per citation, since it's about the issue's own text rather than a
cross-reference): something like *"does the remaining design work reduce to running
one specific, already-named test or experiment whose result has an already-stated
consequence for each outcome, rather than requiring further judgment to decide what to
do?"* A high answer would let `route` report e.g. `sonnet — pending one bounded spike`
instead of folding a spike indistinguishably into the stage tier. Needs the same kind
of live round #1812 ran for `could_be_cheaper` (redacted/simulated-resolved text,
checked against a human reading, checked for confounds) before the wording is trusted
— explicitly **not** done here; this issue proposes the direction, not validated
wording.

## Non-goals

- Not feeding an issue's linked ADR content into the existing stage questions —
  `docs/jev.md` already documents that feeding cross-issue content in made routing
  *worse* (#1812's Motivation section, agreement 12/16 → 9/16). Item 4 is deliberately
  a separate, narrowly-scoped question rather than widening what the stage questions
  see.
- Not auto-detecting spikes by keyword matching ("TODO: verify", "unknown", etc.) —
  too easy to both false-positive on hedging language and false-negative on a spike
  described without those words. If item 4 ships, it goes through Jev like
  `could_be_cheaper` does, not a local heuristic.

## Open questions & caveats

- Items 1, 2 and 4 all need a live-evidence validation round against real issues
  before any wording ships, per this project's own standard for Jev question wording
  (every question here — the stage questions, `verify-decision`'s splitter,
  `could_be_cheaper` itself — has been bitten by an unvalidated first draft at least
  once; see #1812's Evidence section for the shape that validation takes). None of
  that validation work is done in this issue; it's a design proposal built from one
  worked case (#1845), not measured evidence.
- Item 3 is the exception: it needs no validation, since it renders data Jev already
  returns rather than asking a new question. Cheapest to ship, and could land ahead of
  the rest.
- Item 2's suppress-vs-label choice is an open question in itself, not resolved here.

## Implementation plan

### 1. Ship the runner-up display independently

- Add one shared stage-answer formatter used by both the compact
  `render_stage_clause` and multiline `render_stage_line` paths. For a stage in
  `close_calls`, show the highest-probability **nonchosen** option and its
  probability, e.g. `opus (0.18, close call — sonnet 0.16)`. Keep the chosen
  answer's existing `confidence` value distinct from the alternatives in
  `probabilities`.
- Pick deterministically when probabilities tie (option name as a stable
  tiebreaker). If Jev provides no usable alternative, retain `close call`
  without inventing a runner-up. Include `none` when it is a genuine design
  alternative and support custom and multi-model tier names.
- Test close and non-close calls in both text layouts, ties, absent
  alternatives, and a multi-ladder report. Keep the JSON schema and Jev
  request unchanged. Update the text-output example in `docs/jev.md`.

### 2. Establish evidence before changing Jev signals

- Assemble a small, documented set of real open issues and citations with a
  human reading recorded before looking at Jev's new answers. Cover real
  blockers, parent trackers/provenance, ambiguous wording, implementation-led
  class choices, bounded experiments with pre-decided branches, and open
  design questions that still require judgment. Include #1845/#1830, but do
  not tune wording to that one pair.
- For each candidate question, record the exact input text, question wording,
  Jev model/version, response, token cost, expected reading, and failures.
  Compare against the existing route result, a redacted-citation or
  simulated-resolved variant where applicable, and a manual reading. Check
  whether adding questions to the same Jev request changes the existing
  stage answers. Repeat ambiguous cases to expose instability.
- Keep linked ADR and other cross-issue content out of `build_route_state`.
  In particular, if #1845's own text does not state both consequences of its
  proposed test, a low or uncertain spike answer is appropriate; a question
  cannot recover facts that were never sent to Jev. Record that limit rather
  than silently broadening the input.
- Do not ship new question wording solely because it fits #1845. Publish the
  cases, observed mismatches, and the final wording in `docs/jev.md`, as was
  done for #1812.

### 3. Add implementation-stage `could_be_cheaper`

- After its wording passes step 2, ask one additional `noul` question per
  open citation about **this issue's remaining implementation work**. Keep
  the existing, validated design wording byte-for-byte; key the two answers
  separately and ask each once per citation, regardless of the number of
  provider ladders.
- Populate `could_be_cheaper: {design: ..., implement: ...}`. Treat missing or
  malformed answers independently: retain the citation and any valid stage
  score, logging the missing answer; omit the entry only when neither score
  is available. Render both scores with explicit stage names so the reader
  can see which stage could get cheaper.
- Test request keys, answer extraction, partial answers, several citations,
  one versus several ladders, JSON serialization, and text output. Document
  that these scores describe possible remaining work, not a recalculated
  route class.

### 4. Label citation relations conservatively

- Prefer labeling over suppressing. Expose a `relation` value such as
  `blocker`, `tracker`, or `unspecified` on each open citation and show it in
  text output. Keep all open citations visible; do not use the label to
  change stage choices or `could_be_cheaper` scores.
- Preserve enough nearby wording for route-specific relation assessment.
  `find_citations` currently deduplicates by target and keeps only the first
  raw match, which can lose a later explicit dependency statement. Handle
  repeated mentions of the same target and sentence scope, including
  negation and quoted text. Keep `verify-decision`'s citation resolution and
  boundary behavior intact.
- Validate proposed relation rules against the step-2 cases before fixing
  them. Use `unspecified` when the text does not support a stronger claim.
  Test blocker, tracker, neutral, conflicting and repeated mentions, and
  ensure the #1845 parent tracker is not presented as a proven blocker.

### 5. Add a bounded-spike signal

- After validating the wording, add one issue-level `noul` question, not one
  per citation or provider ladder. It should score whether a **specific,
  bounded empirical test** remains and the action for each possible result
  is already stated in the routed issue's text. A named test with undecided
  consequences must not count as a settled fork.
- Add the result as a separate explanation in structured and text output.
  Do not silently lower `stage_design`, `class`, or a provider tier based on
  this score. Choose any high-score label or display threshold from the
  validation results rather than an arbitrary first draft.
- Test one question per issue, absence/partial answers, high and low cases,
  and preservation of the existing stage results. Document what the signal
  does and what missing linked context prevents it from knowing.

### Release checks

- Land step 1 separately if useful; gate steps 3–5 on the recorded live
  evidence in step 2. The relation schema and final spike wording remain
  subject to those results.
- Run focused Rust tests, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
  `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the applicable full test
  suite from this worktree. Review example output and JSON/YAML compatibility.
  Update `docs/jev.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` for shipped behavior.

comments.body:
## First uncertainty-reduction pass (2026-09-22)

### What is ready

Item 3 (runner-up in text output) is implemented in PR #1873. It changes only rendering, with no new Jev question. Focused route tests (88), formatting, Clippy, build, and a live #1871 text-output run passed. The live result included `design needs no further work (0.21, close call — sol 0.39)`.

### The current route choice is unstable near `none`/`sol`

The reported run above chose `sol` for design (confidence 0.21). Three further identical `jev-1.13.0` runs on #1871 using the OpenAI ladder chose `none` (confidence 0.34, 0.24, 0.26). Their `P(none)`/`P(sol)` pairs were 0.50/0.34, 0.43/0.39 and 0.45/0.37. The post-build live smoke run also chose `none` (confidence 0.21, runner-up `sol` 0.39). This is a close boundary, not evidence that editing the plan definitively removed all design work. The OpenAI ladder itself remains unvalidated as documented in `docs/jev.md`.

### Candidate implementation-stage question: preliminary, do not ship yet

I tested a direct adaptation of the existing design `could_be_cheaper` question against current issue text (title, body, comments), with Jev pinned to `jev-1.13.0`. It asks whether resolving the citation would leave less implementation work for **this** issue, assuming design is already done. Human readings were set before looking at the scores.

| Routed issue → citation | Prior reading | `could_be_cheaper.implement` |
|---|---|---:|
| rust-works/succinctly#1356 → rust-works/succinctly#1129 | Explicit blocker; implementation bearing plausible | 0.47 |
| rust-works/succinctly#1343 → rust-works/succinctly#2063 | Implementation-only caveat; modest bearing | 0.51 |
| rust-works/succinctly#1998 → rust-works/succinctly#1419 | Parallel/sibling scope; low bearing | 0.39 |
| rust-works/succinctly#1740 → rust-works/succinctly#1753 | Work absorbed by the cited issue; high bearing | 0.82 |
| omni-dev#1845 → #1830 | Parent tracker, not a blocker | 0.32 |
| omni-dev#1871 → #1845 | Worked-example provenance, not a blocker | 0.23 |

The absorbed case separates clearly, but the middle scores overlap. These are single runs on current text, not the resolved-simulation check used in #1812 or forward validation. In particular, rust-works/succinctly#1356's explicit blocker only scored 0.47. Keep the implementation question out of the product until the simulated-resolved comparison and repeated ambiguous cases are done. The exact candidate question was:

> This issue cites `<CITATION>`, which is still open. If `<CITATION>` is resolved, how likely is it that LESS implementation work (code, tests and docs) would remain for THIS issue than the current text implies — as opposed to this issue own remaining implementation work being unaffected because it is already scoped separately, is a parallel or sibling effort, or `<CITATION>` is otherwise not a precondition for finishing this issue own remaining work? Assume any remaining design work has been completed well.

### Candidate spike question: scope matters

I compared three `noul` wordings. The #1845 "pre-probe" state was reconstructed from its first plan comment without the later resolution; it is **not** an exact archived route input. #1843's pre-probe state used its body and first plan comment. The current/resolved cases used today's title, body and comments. All calls used `jev-1.13.0`.

| Input | Strict "remaining design reduces to one test" | Broad "has a pending test" | Own-issue pending-fork wording |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| #1845 pre-probe plan | 0.33 | 0.94 | 0.90 (repeat 0.89) |
| #1845 after probe | 0.19 | 0.24 | 0.11 |
| #1871 (describes #1845 as an example) | 0.16 | **0.78 false positive** | 0.06 (repeat 0.06) |
| rust-works/succinctly#1998 | 0.06 | 0.18 | 0.20 |
| #1843 pre-probe plan | not run | not run | 0.82 |

The strict question missed the historical #1845 case. The broad question confused #1871's worked example with a spike in #1871's own work. The own-issue wording avoided that confound in this small set. #1843 also still had a separate judgment call, so a high result can only mean **a bounded spike exists**; it must not claim that all design work is gone or lower the chosen tier.

The tested own-issue wording was:

> For THIS issue's own remaining design work (not a worked example, quoted case, cited issue, or proposed feature), is there a specific empirical check that has not yet been run and for which THIS issue already states the concrete action to take for each relevant result? Score high only if performing that check directly settles a live design fork in THIS issue without further architectural judgment. Score low if the check is already complete, merely an example, or additional design judgment is still needed.

This is a promising candidate, not ship-ready wording. It still needs more real positive and negative issues, a batched-question drift check against the existing stage answers, and human review of false positives before choosing a display threshold.

### Citation relation decision

Choose **labeling, not suppression**: keep every open citation visible, with `blocker`, `tracker`, or `unspecified` only when the citing context supports that label. Hiding a genuine dependency is a worse failure than showing an `unspecified` reference. A parent tracker such as #1845→#1830 should not be described as a blocker; #1871→#1845 is example provenance and should stay `unspecified` unless a more precise label earns its own evidence. Before implementation, test repeated references (the current scanner keeps only the first), sentence scope, negation and quoted text against real issues. No local keyword rule is approved by these six cases alone.

### Remaining gates

1. Compare implementation-stage scores with hand-edited resolved simulations, repeat borderline cases, and check the effect of batching the new question with stage questions.

doc.title: refactor(drive): adopt truncate_locations across the remaining sheets previews
doc.body:
## Context

#1872 (`trim-whitespace`, #1844) added `grid_range::truncate_locations`, which renders an A1 address list and elides past a limit (`RENDERED_LOCATION_LIMIT`, 50):

```
  1284 non-blank cell(s) may be trimmed: A1, A2, … (50 shown) … and 1234 more
```

Only the **rendered** line is elided — the structured `-o json` outcome and the `drivemutation` record keep the full list, so nothing a machine reads is lost.

It was added there because `trim-whitespace --whole-sheet` can name every non-blank cell in a tab, where every earlier preview described a paste destination or a merge. It was deliberately **not** retrofitted onto the existing verbs in that PR, to keep the change reviewable. That retrofit is this issue.

## Sites still joining an unbounded list

| site | shape | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_fill.rs:840` | `overwritten_cells.join(", ")` | one long line |
| `text_to_columns.rs:889` | `overwritten_cells.join(", ")` | one long line |
| `paste.rs:1026` | `lines.extend(locations.iter()…)` | **one output line per address** — a wide `copy-paste` destination prints thousands of lines |
| `format.rs:1065` | `discarded_cells.join("; ")` | `merge-cells`, and the entries are `"A1: value"` — see below |
| `named_range.rs:816` area | referencing formula locations | bounded by formulas naming the range; smallest risk |

`paste.rs` is arguably the worst of these, since a line per address scrolls the useful summary off the terminal entirely.

## The one that needs a decision, not a retrofit

`merge-cells` (`format.rs`) is the **only** preview in the integration that prints cell *contents* — ADR-0078 §4 made it the deliberate outlier, and ADR-0077 §5 drew the "no cell content ever appears" line for everything else. Truncating it is therefore not a cosmetic change: it decides how much of the data a merge would discard the operator gets to see before confirming.

Options worth stating explicitly rather than defaulting:

- Leave `merge-cells` uncapped, on the grounds that its whole purpose is to show what is about to be lost, and a merge range is caller-chosen and usually small.
- Cap it with a much higher limit than the address-only previews, since each entry is longer but the information is more valuable per entry.
- Cap it identically and accept that a very large merge preview stops being exhaustive.

The address-only sites have no such tension and can simply adopt the helper.

## Suggested shape

- Move the limit into one place (it currently lives beside `truncate_locations` in `grid_range.rs`) and have the address-only sites call it.
- `paste.rs` needs the small extra step of collapsing its per-line rendering into the joined-and-elided form, which is also what makes its output consistent with its siblings.
- Decide `merge-cells` separately and record the reasoning wherever it lands, since it is an ADR-0078 §4 question rather than a formatting one.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Implementation plan (triage)

### Current state (main @ 800a10cc)

- The helper already exists: `src/drive/sheets/grid_range.rs` has `pub(crate) const RENDERED_LOCATION_LIMIT: usize = 50` (line ~141) and `pub(crate) fn truncate_locations(locations: &[String], limit: usize) -> String` (line ~151), with two unit tests. Its doc comment still says "Every preview before issue #1844 joined its whole list", which this issue makes out of date.
- Callers today: `trim_whitespace.rs::candidate_line` only. `docs/drive.md` (~line 2087) documents the elision for `trim-whitespace` only.
- The sites named in the issue are all still unbounded on main (re-checked by grep; no sheets verb added since introduces another):
  | site | function | shape today |
  |---|---|---|
  | `src/drive/sheets/auto_fill.rs:840` | `overwritten_line` | `overwritten_cells.join(", ")` |
  | `src/drive/sheets/text_to_columns.rs:889` | `overwritten_line` | `overwritten_cells.join(", ")` |
  | `src/drive/sheets/paste.rs:1026` | destination-overwrite block in the change-lines builder | a header line, then **one line per address** (`"    {loc}"`) |
  | `src/drive/sheets/paste.rs:1049` | source-cleared block, same builder (`cut-paste`) | one line per address. **The issue's table misses this one.** |
  | `src/drive/sheets/named_range.rs:1004` | `referencing_formula_lines` | one line per location (`"  {loc}"`) after a count header |
  | `src/drive/sheets/format.rs:1065` | `describe_effect`, `MergeCells` arm | `discarded_cells.join("; ")`, entries are `"A1: value"` |
- Structured outputs (`-o json` outcomes, `drivemutation` records) already carry the full lists and are **not** touched by this change.

### Approach

1. **One helper, one limit.** Keep `truncate_locations` and `RENDERED_LOCATION_LIMIT` in `grid_range.rs` (it is already the shared module every verb imports). Add a thin convenience wrapper so callers don't repeat the constant:
   ```rust
   pub(crate) fn render_locations(locations: &[String]) -> String {
       truncate_locations(locations, RENDERED_LOCATION_LIMIT)
   }
   ```
   and switch `trim_whitespace.rs::candidate_line` to it too. Update the doc comment to say it is the one rendering path for every address-list preview (#1844 introduced it, #1880 adopted it everywhere).
2. **Address-only sites adopt it verbatim:** `auto_fill.rs::overwritten_line`, `text_to_columns.rs::overwritten_line` replace `.join(", ")` with `grid_range::render_locations(..)`. Their "N non-blank cell(s)" count already comes from `.len()`, so the total stays exact.
3. **`paste.rs` collapses per-line output into one joined line** for both the destination block and the cleared-source block, matching the siblings:
   `  2 non-blank cell(s) in the destination would be overwritten: D1, D2` and `  4 non-blank cell(s) in the source will be cleared: A1, …`. This is the "worst" site (thousands of lines scroll the summary away) and the change also makes its format consistent with `auto-fill`/`text-to-columns`.
4. **`named_range.rs::referencing_formula_lines`** — same collapse: keep the count sentence ("N cell formula(s) reference this name and will start evaluating to #NAME? once …") and append `: <render_locations>` (or put the list on one following indented line if the sentence is already long; implementer's choice, keep one line of addresses). Entries are sheet-qualified (`'Q1'!A1`), which the helper handles unchanged. ADR-0081 §2 requires the preview to be *mandatory*, not exhaustive-in-text; the JSON keeps the full list, so eliding the rendered line is consistent — note this in the doc comment.
5. **`merge-cells` — decision: leave uncapped (option 1), and record why.** Rationale:
   - ADR-0078 §4 makes this preview the *substitute for a confirmation flag* and says it "names exactly what would be lost"; eliding it would silently weaken that guarantee, which is an ADR change, not a formatting one.
   - The list only ever contains non-top-left, non-blank cells of a caller-chosen merge range, which in practice is small; the pathological cases the helper exists for (`--whole-sheet`, wide paste destinations) don't arise.
   - It is already one line (not one line per entry), so it cannot scroll the summary off-screen the way `paste` does.
   Record it as: a short comment at `format.rs` `MergeCells` arm ("deliberately not elided — ADR-0078 §4 / #1880"), plus one sentence appended to ADR-0078 §4 (an in-place clarification, not a new ADR — no decision changes). If the maintainer prefers a cap instead, the fallback is option 2: a separate `MERGE_DISCARD_RENDER_LIMIT` (e.g. 200) via `truncate_locations`-style logic with `"; "` as the separator — that would need `truncate_locations` to take a separator, so don't generalise it unless option 2 is chosen.

### File-by-file changes

- `src/drive/sheets/grid_range.rs`: add `render_locations`, refresh doc comment; unit test that `render_locations` elides at exactly 51 entries (`"… and 1 more"`) and not at 50.
- `src/drive/sheets/trim_whitespace.rs`: use `render_locations` (no behaviour change).
- `src/drive/sheets/auto_fill.rs`: `overwritten_line` → `render_locations`; add a test with 60 overwritten cells asserting `… and 10 more` in the rendered line and 60 entries in the outcome.
- `src/drive/sheets/text_to_columns.rs`: same as auto_fill.
- `src/drive/sheets/paste.rs`: collapse both blocks (destination ~1020–1027, cleared ~1036–1050) into single lines; update the existing test near line 2846 (`rendered.contains("    D1")`) to the new single-line form; add an elision test for a >50-cell destination and for `cut-paste`'s cleared list. Keep the test that asserts no cell *values* leak (ADR-0077 §5).
- `src/drive/sheets/named_range.rs`: `referencing_formula_lines` collapse + elision; update any test asserting the per-line layout (search `referencing_formula_lines` / `"  'Q1'!A1"` in its tests).
- `src/drive/sheets/format.rs`: comment only (merge-cells stays uncapped).
- `docs/adrs/adr-0078.md` §4: one clarifying sentence that the rendered discard list is intentionally never elided (#1880), unlike the address-only previews.
- `docs/drive.md`: generalise the "Past 50 addresses the rendered line elides the remainder (`… and N more`); the `-o json` outcome keeps the full list" note — either repeat it at the auto-fill (~1900), text-to-columns (~1975), copy/cut-paste, and delete-named-range sections, or add it once in the shared Sheets preview conventions section and link to it. Update any paste example that shows the per-line layout (none found on main, but re-check).
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` → `### Changed`: rendered previews of `auto-fill`, `text-to-columns`, `copy-paste`/`cut-paste` and `delete-named-range` now elide address lists past 50 (`… and N more`); `copy-paste`/`cut-paste` print addresses on one line instead of one per line; `-o json` and mutation records unchanged; `merge-cells` deliberately unchanged.

### CLI surface / snapshots

No clap flags or help text change, so `help_all_output.snap` is unaffected. Run `cargo insta test` anyway in case any sheets integration snapshot captures rendered preview text; accept only diffs matching the intended one-line/elided form.

### Risks / open questions

- **Scriptability of text output:** someone parsing `paste`'s one-address-per-line text output would break. Acceptable — `-o json` is the machine surface and is unchanged; call it out in the CHANGELOG.
- **merge-cells decision** is the only judgment call; the plan picks "uncapped" with recorded reasoning. Maintainer can flip to option 2 before implementation.
- Commit scope: `drive` (plus `docs`/`changelog` as needed); lint with `omni-dev git commit message lint`.

### PR breakdown

Single PR — small, localized, all in `src/drive/sheets/` plus docs.

**Recommended model:** Sonnet — mechanical adoption of an existing helper at five well-identified call sites with clear test updates; the one design question (merge-cells) is resolved in this plan.

doc.title: ai jev route/verify-decision: cache GitHub issue fetches to avoid redundant re-querying
doc.body:
`omni-dev ai jev route` and `verify-decision` each fetch their GitHub issues/PRs
by shelling out directly to `gh api graphql` (`src/github_issues.rs::fetch_items`
→ `pr_status::run_gh_graphql`), once per CLI invocation, with no caching layer.
Both humans iterating (re-running `route` while tuning `--ladders`, re-running
`verify-decision` while tuning the splitter prompt) and AI agents driving the
CLI repeatedly are likely to re-query the same issue/PR/comment thread within
a short window, each time paying a fresh GraphQL round trip (and rate-limit
budget) for identical data.

## What

Add a caching layer so repeated `route`/`verify-decision` invocations against
the same issue reuse a recent fetch instead of re-hitting the GitHub API:

- Most likely shape: a small TTL'd cache keyed by `ItemRef`
  (owner/repo/number), served by the **daemon** — following the precedent
  already in `src/daemon/services/worktrees.rs`'s `TreeSnapshotCache` /
  `PrBadge` staleness handling, and the existing `github_metrics::run_gh`
  call-counting choke point that both worktrees and `github_issues.rs`
  already funnel through.
- `route`/`verify-decision` would become daemon socket clients for this fetch,
  with a **required fallback to today's direct `gh api graphql` path** when
  the daemon isn't running — mirroring `worktrees rebase`'s local-fallback
  design — so neither command gains a hard daemon dependency.
- Alternative worth weighing first: a simpler flat-file TTL cache (no daemon
  involvement), similar in spirit to the request log's on-disk state. Lower
  complexity, but doesn't dedupe concurrent invocations across processes the
  way a resident daemon cache would, and doesn't reuse the rate-limit
  awareness (`github_rate_limit`, `WARN_PERCENT`) that already lives in the
  daemon.

## Why now

Not urgent — no reported rate-limit incident yet — but `route`/`verify-decision`
are new (#1779, #1787) and their expected usage pattern (iterative tuning by
both humans and AI agents) makes redundant re-fetching likely enough to be
worth designing for before it becomes a real API budget problem.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Plan

### Decision: flat-file TTL cache, not a daemon service

The issue offers two shapes. This plan picks the **flat-file cache** for these reasons:

- **The usage pattern the issue names is sequential.** A human or agent re-runs `route` or `verify-decision` against the same issue while tuning flags or prompts. A shared on-disk cache catches every repeat after the first. The one thing a daemon adds is deduplicating *concurrent in-flight* fetches, and the issue gives no evidence that happens.
- **No daemon fallback path.** A daemon cache would need a new socket op, wire DTOs, a daemon-down fallback to the direct `gh` path (so two code paths to test), and version-skew handling. A file cache has one path, and it degrades to today's behaviour on any I/O error.
- **`gh` already owns the token and the rate limit.** Fetches still go through `github_metrics::run_gh`/`run_gh_graphql`, so they're counted and logged as today. A cache hit makes no call, so it spends no budget. Reusing the daemon's `github_rate_limit` warning buys little here.
- **Reversible.** If concurrent dedupe ever matters, the daemon can later serve the same per-item entries. The cache API (`IssueCache`) is the seam either way.

### Shape

New module `src/github_issues/cache.rs` (`mod cache;` from `github_issues.rs`, re-exporting `IssueCache`):

- **Key:** one entry per item, `(project, number)`. The path is `<cache_dir>/omni-dev/github-issues/<owner>/<repo>/<number>.json`, with `cache_dir` from `dirs::cache_dir()`. An owner or repo segment that isn't `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` (or is `.`/`..`) disables caching for that ref instead of building a path from it.
- **Entry:** `{"schema": 1, "fetched_at": <unix secs>, "doc": IssueDoc}`. `IssueDoc` is already `Serialize`/`Deserialize`. A missing, unparseable, old-schema or expired entry is a **miss** (debug log), never an error.
- **Shared across both fetchers.** `fetch_issues` (the `issue(number:)` query) and `fetch_items` (`issueOrPullRequest`) build byte-identical `IssueDoc`s for an issue, so they share entries:
  - `fetch_items` accepts any cached kind.
  - `fetch_issues` accepts only `kind == Issue`. A cached PR is a miss, so the network path still produces today's "is a pull request" error.
- **Not-found results are never cached**, so fixing a typo or granting `gh` access takes effect at once.
- **Writes are best-effort:** dir `0700`, file `0600`, written through `tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in` then `persist` (atomic, and no temp-name collision between concurrent processes). A write failure is logged at `debug` and never fails the command.
- **TTL:** `OMNI_DEV_GITHUB_CACHE_TTL_SECS`, read through `SettingsEnv` so `settings.json` and profiles work too. Default **300 s**. `0` disables the cache entirely (no reads, no writes). A malformed value warns and falls back to the default (STYLE-0018).
  - Why 300 s: long enough to cover rapid re-runs, short enough that a freshly posted decision comment is seen soon. `--refresh` covers the "I just commented" case immediately.
- **API:**
  - `IssueCache::from_env()`, a thin wrapper over `IssueCache::new(dir: Option<PathBuf>, ttl: Duration, refresh: bool)`. `from_env_with(&impl EnvSource, base_dir, refresh)` is the STYLE-0028 seam, and `IssueCache::disabled()` is for tests and callers.
  - New `fetch_issues_cached(bin, cache, refs)` / `fetch_items_cached(bin, cache, refs)`: serve hits from disk, fetch only the misses through the existing uncached `fetch_issues`/`fetch_items` (unchanged, so their tests stand), write the fresh docs back, and return results in caller order.
- **Visibility of reuse:** the cache counts hits and the oldest reused age. The CLI prints one stderr line when anything was reused, e.g. `note: reused 3 cached GitHub item(s), up to 2m old; pass --refresh to re-fetch`, so stale input is never silent. (This goes to stderr; stdout JSON/YAML stays unchanged.)

### CLI surface

- `ai jev route --refresh` and `ai jev verify-decision --refresh` re-fetch everything instead of reading the cache. The fresh copies are still written.
- `fetch_docs`/`find_open_dependencies` (route), `fetch_verify_input` (verify) and `fetch_input` (verify CLI) take `&IssueCache`. Existing tests pass `&IssueCache::disabled()`.
- Out of scope: `resolve_current_project` (`gh repo view`) and `list_open_issue_numbers` (`--all-open`'s listing, which must be fresh). The per-issue docs `--all-open` then fetches *are* cached.

### Tests

- Cache unit tests: round trip, TTL expiry (backdated `fetched_at`), schema mismatch or corrupt file is a miss, `refresh` skips reads but still writes, TTL 0 neither reads nor writes, unsafe path segments aren't cached, a PR entry is not served to `fetch_issues`, file mode `0600`, and env parsing via `MapEnv` (default, `0`, malformed).
- Fake-gh shim tests: a second `fetch_*_cached` call makes **no** `gh` call (the shim counts invocations), and a mixed hit/miss batch fetches only the misses and preserves order.
- Update clap parse tests for `--refresh`, and the `help_all` snapshot via the `update-snapshots` skill.

### Docs

- `docs/jev.md`: a "GitHub fetch cache" section covering the path, TTL env var, `--refresh`, what is and isn't cached, the stderr note, and that private-repo issue text is stored `0600` under the user cache dir. Add a CLAUDE.md Jev-section line and a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.

doc.title: yq: tonumber drops non-JSON spellings (+2.0, 007, 2., .5) that real yq echoes verbatim
doc.body:
**Severity: Low**

## Summary

#1090 made `tonumber` preserve a JSON-shaped number's source spelling. Spellings YAML/yq accept but strict RFC 8259 rejects still fall through to a plain `Int`/`Float` and lose their text.

```
$ printf 'a: "+2.0"\n' | yq '.b = (.a|tonumber)'    # real yq
a: "+2.0"
b: +2.0
$ printf 'a: "+2.0"\n' | succinctly yq '.b = (.a|tonumber)'
a: "+2.0"
b: 2.0
```

Full set (`succinctly yq` vs yq v4.53.3):

| input | real yq | succinctly |
|---|---|---|
| `"+2.0"` | `+2.0` | `2.0` |
| `"007"`  | `007`  | `7` |
| `"2."`   | `2.`   | `2.0` |
| `".5"`   | `.5`   | `0.5` |

jq mode is **not** affected — real jq 1.7.1 normalizes all four the same way succinctly does (`7`, `0.5`, `2.0`), and those cases match today.

## Why it is not simply fixed

A `NumberLiteral`'s stored text is re-read *as JSON* by `to_json_for_reindex`'s reindex bridge, so a non-JSON-safe spelling cannot be stored verbatim without corrupting that round trip. `src/yaml/scalar.rs`'s `preservable_float_literal_text` documents this exact constraint for the YAML-input side, and normalizes (`+1.0` -> `1.0`, `1.` -> `1.0`, `007e2` -> `7e2`) rather than preserving.

`tonumber` already applies the one normalization that has an exact JSON equivalent — stripping a leading `+` — because real jq wants `2.0` there. The remaining three have no JSON-safe equivalent that keeps the original bytes.

This is the same permanent-divergence class `preservable_float_literal_text` already records for `-o yaml`/`tostring`/`join` on document-sourced `+1.0`/`1.`/`007e2`. Fixing it properly means the stored spelling and the bridge's JSON text stop being the same string.

## Suggested direction

Either accept and document alongside the existing `preservable_float_literal_text` divergence note, or give `NumberLiteral` a separate "display text" distinct from its "bridge text". The latter is a real design change and should be weighed against the rest of the number-fidelity cluster (#1076, #1129, #1144).

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Triage (2026-09-04) — blocked on #1129's classifier change (D2); the fork is decided: store verbatim, normalise at JSON emission

Re-verified on `147fc1638`: all four rows in the body still diverge (`+2.0`->`2.0`, `007`->`7`, `2.`->`!!float 2`, `.5`->`0.5`). Also: yq's `tonumber` re-resolves with its YAML reader — `"0x10"|tonumber` -> `0x10` (`!!int`, `+0` -> 16), `"1_000"|tonumber` -> `1_000`; succinctly errors on both. jq mode is correct and must stay (real jq 1.7.1 normalises: `"+2.0"`->`2.0`, `"2."`->`2`, `"007"`->`7`).

**Decision (see the cluster comment on #1144, D2):** not a second "display text" field. `NumberLiteral` keeps the verbatim spelling; every JSON emitter (and the reindex bridge's `NumberLiteral` arm) goes through one `yq_json_number_text(repr, text)` implementing yq's own `jsonFloatLiteral` rule (echo iff RFC-8259 grammar and has `.` or exponent; else `FormatFloat` + `.0`). Once #1129 lands that, this issue is: give `tonumber_from_str` an `S: EvalSemantics` parameter; in yq mode resolve the trimmed string with `resolve_plain` and keep the text (`+2.0`, `007`, `2.`, `.5`, `0x10`); `-o=json` then prints `2.0`, `7`, `2.0`, `0.5`, `16` — matching yq. `1_000` stays `!!str` here (YAML 1.1 underscore digits are a recorded input-spec divergence; do not chase).

Residual to record in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`: a spelling the JSON reader cannot represent loses its text when it crosses the reindex bridge (`+2.0`->`2.0`, `0x10`->`16`, `2.`->`2.0`); `007`/`.5`/overflow digit runs survive via the existing leniency arms. Stays in Todo until #1129 lands.

doc.title: yq: -s/--eval-all/-i bypass #868's paths/leaf_paths duplicate-key fix
doc.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #868 (fixed by #1341, cursor-native `paths`/`leaf_paths` arms in `eval_generic.rs`'s dispatch). That fix only helps the default (non-slurp, non-inplace, single-document) evaluation path. Several other CLI invocation modes still route `paths`/`leaf_paths` through `eval.rs`'s old, un-fixed `to_owned`-based `builtin_paths`/`builtin_leaf_paths` instead, and so still silently collapse duplicate YAML mapping keys — even for the exact bare `paths`/`leaf_paths` shapes #1341 fixed on the default path.

## Repro (all against `printf 'a: 1\na: 2\nb: 3\n'`)

Default path (fixed by #1341):
```
$ succinctly yq '[paths]'
[["a"],["a"],["b"]]
```

`-s`/`--slurp` with a non-identity filter (bypasses the fix — `can_slurp_fast_path` requires `is_identity`):
```
$ succinctly yq -s 'paths'
- 0
- 0
- a
- 0
- b
```
(Should include `[0,"a"]` twice; only once.)

`--eval-all` (no fast path exists at all for this mode):
```
$ succinctly yq --eval-all 'paths'
- 0
---
- 0
- a
---
- 0
- b
```
(Same collapse.)

`-i`/`--inplace` (bypasses the fix — `can_use_m2_streaming` doesn't recognize `Builtin::Paths`/`Builtin::LeafPaths` as m2-streamable, so `can_inplace_fast_path` never fires):
```
$ printf 'a: 1\na: 2\nb: 3\n' > f.yaml && succinctly yq -i 'paths' f.yaml && cat f.yaml
- a
- b
```
(Same collapse; `-i '.'` on the same file correctly preserves both `a:` lines, since identity *is* m2-streamable.)

## Why this needs its own fix

All three modes (`-s` non-identity, `--eval-all`, `-i`) parse the whole document into an `OwnedValue` up front (`parse_input`/`yaml_to_owned_value`) before evaluating, then dispatch through `eval.rs`'s own evaluator (`jq::eval::<_, YqSemantics>`), landing in the pre-`#1341` `builtin_paths`/`builtin_leaf_paths` regardless of what `eval_generic.rs` now does. Closing this gap needs either:
- teaching `eval.rs`'s own `collect_paths`/`collect_leaf_paths` (the `OwnedValue`-based versions) to be duplicate-key-aware too (they currently walk an `OwnedValue::Object`'s `IndexMap` directly, which has already collapsed duplicates by the time `to_owned`/`yaml_to_owned_value` produced it) — likely requiring a duplicate-key-preserving `OwnedValue` representation, a larger change; or
- extending `can_slurp_fast_path`/`can_use_m2_streaming` to recognize `Builtin::Paths`/`Builtin::LeafPaths` as fast-pathable so they route through the already-fixed `eval_generic.rs` dispatch instead.

Filed separately from #1342 (the `paths(node_filter)` follow-up) since the root cause and fix location are different — this is a CLI-invocation-mode routing gap, not a missing native-arm gap.

doc.title: yq: YamlValue::key_string's "" fallback would collapse two different keys under jq-mode collapse
doc.body:
**Severity: Low** (latent, not currently reachable) — noted while working #1642, not filed
at the time.

## Summary

`YamlValue::key_string()` (`src/yaml/light.rs:6154-6169`) returns the literal empty string
`""` for any key with no scalar form — a complex/non-scalar key (issue #222), and, since
#1642, a key whose bytes fail to *decode* too (`document::key_display_string` falls back to
`Cow::Borrowed("")` for any `DocumentValue` whose `key_raw_source_span()` is `None`, which
it always is for YAML — there is no raw-span concept there, unlike JSON).

The identity/collapse machinery that decides whether two fields share a name for jq-mode's
duplicate-key-collapses rule (`collapse_repeated`/`collapse_confirmed_repeat`/
`DistinctKeyCursors` in `src/jq/document.rs`) keys off `key_string()`/`key_hash_of()`
directly. If **two different** such YAML keys in one mapping both stringify to `""` (e.g.
two distinct complex keys, or two different-but-both-undecodable scalar keys), and this
mapping were ever evaluated under `S::COLLAPSE_DUPLICATE_KEYS = true` (`JqSemantics`),
the collapse machinery would treat both `""`-keyed fields as *the same* key and silently
collapse them to one — the exact class of bug #1642 fixed for JSON's analogous case
(`key_hash_of`/`DistinctKeyCursors` staying `None`-safe for a JSON decode-failure key was
the fix's whole point; YAML's `""` convention sidesteps `None` entirely by always
succeeding, which is safe only because nothing collapses it today).

## Why this is not live today

Confirmed by reading the call graph, not by reproducing a failure: `YamlValue` is only ever
evaluated under `YqSemantics` (`COLLAPSE_DUPLICATE_KEYS = false`) in the shipped binary.
`src/bin/succinctly/jq_runner.rs` never references `YamlValue`/`YamlIndex` at all, and
`yq_runner.rs`'s own `--input-format json` bridge (`to_owned_canonicalizing_numbers`,
added alongside #1642's fix) pairs `StandardJson` with `YqSemantics` — the *other*
direction, JSON read but evaluated in yq mode, not YAML read but evaluated in jq mode. So
there is no live path today that pairs `YamlValue` with `JqSemantics`, and this is
currently unreachable.

## Suggested direction (not attempted)

Either:
1. Give `YamlValue` its own `key_raw_source_span` in the same spirit as JSON's (a raw
   scalar-node byte span, when one exists) so a decode-failure YAML key gets a
   distinguishing fallback instead of a shared `""` — closing the gap the same way #1642
   closed it for JSON, symmetric across formats even though only one side is reachable
   today; or
2. Leave `""` as-is (matching the pre-existing #222 convention for genuinely complex keys,
   which has the identical property) and instead assert in code — a debug assertion or a
   type-level constraint — that `YamlValue` and `JqSemantics` are never paired, so a future
   change that introduces such a pairing fails loudly instead of silently reintroducing
   this class of bug.

## Related

- #1642 — the JSON-side fix this gap mirrors; see its "YAML" section in the PR/commit
  history for the original context this was noted in.
- #222 — established the `""` convention for a YAML key with no scalar form, which this
  issue's collision risk is really about (the decode-failure case just widened how often
  the convention fires).

doc.title: yq: sort/sort_by's path-tracked error wording, and .[] read-side scalar no-op, need their own fixes
doc.body:
## Summary

Found alongside #1901 (any/all/flatten/group_by/unique/unique_by/from_entries's own error-wording fix, PR to follow). Two more real-yq divergences confirmed live against pinned Homebrew yq v4.53.3, both explicitly scoped OUT of that PR because they need materially different implementation shapes than a simple wording swap.

## 1. `sort`/`sort_by` on a non-array/map: real yq's wording names a genuine navigation path

```console
$ printf 'null\n' | yq '5 | sort'
Error: node at path [] is not an array or map (it's a !!int)
$ printf '{"a": {"b": 5}}\n' | yq '.a.b | sort'
Error: node at path [a.b] is not an array or map (it's a !!int)
$ printf '[1,2,5]\n' | yq '.[2] | sort'
Error: node at path [[2]] is not an array or map (it's a !!int)
```

The `<path>` portion genuinely varies with navigation depth (`[]` at top level, `[a.b]` after `.a.b`, `[[2]]` after `.[2]`) -- unlike #1901's seven builtins, whose wording never names a path at all. `builtin_sort`/`builtin_sort_by` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) receive only a bare value with no path context today, so fixing this needs real path-tracking plumbing threaded into these builtins, not just a wording constant.

`sort_by` uses the identical message shape (same repro pattern, confirmed live).

## 2. `.[]`'s own read-side behavior on a scalar: real yq treats it as a silent no-op

```console
$ printf 'null\n' | yq '5 | .[]'
                                          # exit 0, no output at all
```

succinctly raises \`cannot_iterate_with\` here in yq mode too, matching jq's own \`.[]\` semantics (correct for jq mode, not yq's read side). Whether this shares one root cause with #1901's seven builtins is unresolved -- bare \`Expr::Iterate\` has 20+ separate dispatch arms across \`src/jq/eval.rs\`'s value-mode, path-mode, and assignment-mode evaluators (confirmed via \`grep -n \"Expr::Iterate =>\"\`), so scoping this properly needs its own investigation into which of those arms is reachable from a bare top-level \`.[]\` on a scalar, and whether the fix should live in one shared place or needs per-mode gating at several sites.

## Scope

Filed as a follow-up rather than folded into #1901/its PR, per that PR's own explicit scope note.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Triage (2026-09-04) — item 2 decided (one EvalSemantics const, two arms); item 1 split into a wording fix now and a path-tracking design later

### Item 1 — `sort`/`sort_by`/`reverse`/`shuffle` path wording
yq's `[path]` is `CandidateNode.GetNicePath()` (operator_sort.go), the node's parent/key lineage —
it survives non-navigation: `.a as $x | $x | sort` → `[a]`, `(.a + 1) | sort` → `[a]`,
`{"z": .a} | .z | sort` → `[z]`, `[.a][0] | sort` → `[[0]]`, `.a[0].b | sort` → `[a[0].b]`.
`reverse`/`shuffle` use `node at path [..] is not an array (it's a !!tag)`; `tonumber` uses
`cannot convert node value [x] at path a.b of tag !!str to number` — same family.
succinctly's path context (`eval.rs::needs_path_context` → `eval_pipe_with_path_context_internal`;
cursor fast path `eval_generic.rs::try_path_context_cursor_walk`, #2061) is mode-agnostic and
re-routes the whole pipe through the OwnedValue evaluator — hooking `sort` into it taxes every yq
`sort` and needs the path threaded into `builtin_sort`'s error. **Decision:**
- 1a (do now, Sonnet): yq-mode arms in `builtin_sort`/`builtin_sort_by`/`builtin_reverse`/`shuffle`
  emitting `node at path [] is not an array or map (it's a !!int)` / `… is not an array (it's a
  !!str)` with the tag right and the path fixed at `[]` — exact for root/literal inputs (`5 | sort`,
  `"s" | reverse`), wrong path text after navigation. Record honestly in
  `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` (`yaml_type_tag` gives the tag). Tests: `5 | sort`,
  `"s" | sort_by(.)`, `null | reverse` (yq: `!!null`).
- 1b (separate issue, needs design): real path text via the cursor walk for navigable prefixes,
  with `[]` fallback for computed inputs; also fixes `tonumber`'s wording. Not Sonnet-sized.

### Item 2 — read-side `.[]` on a scalar
yq is uniformly silent on any *read* traversal of a scalar: on `a: 5`, `.a[]`, `.a.b`, `.a[0]`,
`.a["k"]` → no output; `[.a.b]` → `[]`; `.a.b // "d"` → `"d"`. succinctly yq errors on each
(`Cannot iterate over number (5)`, `Cannot index number with string "b"`). Writes already no-op.
**Decision:** add `EvalSemantics::SCALAR_TRAVERSE_IS_NOOP: bool` (Yq `true`, Jq `false`) and
consult it at exactly the two read arms a bare `.[]` reaches — `eval_generic.rs::eval_single`'s
`Expr::Iterate` else-branch (cursor path, what `.a[]` hits) and `eval.rs::eval_single`'s
`Expr::Iterate` `_ =>` arm (bridged `5 | .[]`) — returning `None` **without** the decode check
(nothing reads the scalar; same reasoning as the yq `map` arm's "content-independent op" comment in
`eval_generic.rs::eval_builtin`). Do the `Field`/`Index`-on-scalar siblings (`.a.b`, `.a[0]`) in the
same PR with the same const — they are the same rule and no open issue owns the read side (#1411/
#1419/#2125 are `del`/assignment). Leave `path_step_generic` and `del` to #1411.
Tests (`tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`): `5 | .[]`, `.a[]`, `[.a.b]` → `[]`, `.a.b // "d"` → `"d"`,
`[5 | .[] | 1]` → `[]`; `tests/jq_cli_tests.rs`: `5 | .[]` still `Cannot iterate over number (5)`.
Pitfall: `null | .[]` is also silent in yq (jq errors) — include null in the const's coverage.

Coordination: item 2's scalar-traverse rule is the *read-side* twin of the path-side rule #1419/#2125 (and #1411's `del` walker) are adding in the same session's triage. Land one shared predicate (`is_yq_field_index_noop_scalar` already exists) and gate every site on it, rather than a second copy — #106's duplicated-predicate lesson.

doc.title: feat(drive): randomizeRange for drive sheets (#1830)
doc.body:
## Plan

State of play: the blocker #1831 closed as [ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md) (numbered 0083, not the 0082 predicted in #1831's own plan comment). Sort-range (#1842, PR #1866), auto-fill (#1840, PR #1862) and text-to-columns (#1843, PR #1867) are all merged, and sort-range is the near-exact template for this verb. This worktree currently sits 12 commits behind `main` and predates sort-range, so step 1 rebases before anything else. No other grid-mutation PR is open right now, so the tracker's two-at-a-time snapshot-collision rule isn't a live constraint.

### What ADR-0083 fixes for this verb
- **§3**: `randomizeRange` joins `sheets-write` alone, on the values-only reading — a permutation of the range's own cells is a strict special case of what a `sheets-write` grant already permits via `clear`+`write`.
- **§6, "nothing discarded" tier**: no `values` read in `--dry-run`. The preview names the range, leads with the range-width-vs-sheet's-allocated-width record-integrity caveat (a narrower selection can silently decouple a record's other columns), then the smaller "references outside the range may see a different row's value" caveat. Never a value, and never a claim of predicting the resulting order — it's server-side randomness.
- **§5**: `randomizeRange` (alongside `sortRange`) is explicitly named as a live-verification item for two open questions: whether the server carries a row's **formatting** with it when moved, and what happens to a **formula inside the range** (moved with its row, references rewritten or not, or left in place). If formatting moves, the ADR's fixed rule requires flipping the gate to **both** `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure` (the text-to-columns precedent, which hit exactly this). Sort-range shipped *without* doing this verification, so this issue is the first time it actually gets answered for the reorder pair — and if the answer is "yes, formatting moves," sort-range's gate needs the same fix as a follow-up.

### Steps

1. **Rebase onto `origin/main`** so `src/drive/sheets/sort_range.rs` and its CLI module are present to mirror.
2. **Wire type** in `src/drive/sheets/types.rs`: `RandomizeRangeRequest { range: GridRange }` plus a `BatchUpdateRequestItem::RandomizeRange` variant, doc comment citing ADR-0083 §3, and a serialization test asserting `{"randomizeRange":{"range":{...}}}`.
3. **Engine** `src/drive/sheets/randomize_range.rs` — a trimmed copy of `sort_range.rs` with the sort-spec machinery removed. Same options struct minus `sort_by`; same result shape (`WouldChange`/`Changed` carrying `range` + `width_warning`); same flow: A1 compose → `target_gate::resolve` on `SheetsWrite` → `spreadsheets.get` → bounded-range refusal → width warning → dry-run returns before any lease/batchUpdate → `LeasedWrite` + `conclude_native_leased_write` for the real run. Log operation `sheets-randomize-range`. Lift the `width_warning` helper out of `sort_range.rs` into a shared `grid_range` helper rather than duplicating it (mirrors how #1843 lifted `non_blank_locations`).
4. **Preview/output wording**: dry-run — "Would randomize the row order of {range} in {book}" plus "the resulting order is chosen by the server and cannot be previewed; the current row order will not be preserved." Real run — "Randomized the row order of {range}" plus the outside-references caveat. No cell contents ever.
5. **CLI** `src/cli/drive/sheets/randomize_range.rs`: `randomize-range <ID> --range <A1> [--sheet NAME] [--dry-run] [lease flag] [-o]`. Register `RandomizeRange` in `SheetsSubcommands` right after `SortRange`, `pub mod` in `src/drive/sheets.rs`. Verb name is 15 chars, well inside the 27-char cap.
6. **Live verification (ADR-0083 §5)** — the step sort-range skipped. Back up `~/.omni-dev/settings.json`, add a temporary `sheets-write`-only rule scoped to the `omni-dev-test` folder, build a sheet with a bold/coloured row and a relative formula inside the target range, randomize it, read back values/formatting, restore settings and md5-verify. Record both findings in `docs/drive.md`:
   - If formatting moves with rows → switch the gate to `target_gate::resolve_all` over both operations, update the `SheetsStructure` doc comment, and file a follow-up issue for sort-range (same defect, different verb).
   - Formula-movement finding → caveat wording only, doesn't move the gate.
7. **Docs/sync**: new `#### drive sheets randomize-range` section in `docs/drive.md` between sort-range and auto-fill; add the verb to the default-policy table's `sheets-write` row; extend `SheetsWrite`'s doc comment in `src/drive/write_gate.rs`; `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry citing #1845 and ADR-0083 §§3, 5, 6.
8. **Tests**, mirroring sort-range's set: request JSON, CLI parse, dry-run makes no `values` read and no batchUpdate, real run sends one `randomizeRange` request, open-ended/unknown-sheet refusals, denied-gate attempt recording, all four lease refusals, every `describe_lines` arm, jsonl output. Then the `update-snapshots` skill for the help golden, and a local `cargo llvm-cov --lib` pass before trusting any posted PR coverage comment.
9. **Ship**: commit as `feat(drive): add sheets randomize-range command`, lint with `omni-dev git commit message lint origin/main..HEAD`, open a PR fixing #1845 citing ADR-0083 §§3, 5, 6, then tick the tracker checkbox in #1830.

### Calls made without asking
- Require a fully bounded range, same as sort-range (`A2:D100`, not `A:A`/`2:2`).
- No confirmation flag (ADR-0075 §3), consistent with the rest of the tranche.

### Flagged for visibility
If step 6's live verification finds that formatting moves with reordered rows, the scope grows beyond this issue alone: it changes this verb's gate to a two-operation composition *and* surfaces that sort-range (#1842, already merged) is mis-gated under the same rule, requiring a follow-up there. That's in-scope per ADR-0083 §5's own fixed rule, not a scope decision I'm making unilaterally.

doc.title: feat(drive): textToColumns for drive sheets (#1830)
doc.body:
## Plan

**Unblocked.** #1831 closed with [ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md) merged, and it settles this verb's three questions by section, so nothing here is a design decision:

- **§1 — gate:** `DriveOperation::SheetsWrite` alone. It writes ordinary cell content into the target sheet; nothing a `sheets clear` + `sheets write` of the same cells could not already do under that grant. It is "the one verb whose destination the caller does not name" — the API writes into however many columns to the right the split needs.
- **§5 — grid edge:** a spill past `columnCount` is **not refused client-side** and the verb **never prepends** an `appendDimension`/`updateSheetProperties` to grow the sheet. Whether the API errors or grows is a live-verification item, recorded in `docs/drive.md`. Second live item with its consequence fixed in advance: if the split is found to carry the source cell's **formatting** into the spill cells, the gate moves to `target_gate::resolve_all([SheetsWrite, SheetsStructure])` (the `add-pivot-table` composition); values-only stays `SheetsWrite`.
- **§6 — `--dry-run`:** first tier, computable **only as an upper bound** ("the API decides how many columns a `textToColumns` split needs"): name the span the write may reach and report the **count and A1 locations** of non-blank cells within it — never a cell's value, never the split pieces. The issue's proposal to "apply the same split logic client-side and report the resulting column layout" is kept for the *width*, not the *contents*.

### API facts (from the `spreadsheets.batchUpdate` reference)

`TextToColumnsRequest { source: GridRange, delimiter: string, delimiterType: enum }`. `source` "must span exactly one column". `delimiterType` ∈ `COMMA | SEMICOLON | PERIOD | SPACE | CUSTOM | AUTODETECT` (plus `DELIMITER_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`, whose behaviour is undocumented, so the flag has no default and the enum has no `Unspecified` variant). `delimiter` is read only under `CUSTOM`. **No response object** — the real run reports what it sent, as `auto-fill` does.

### Surface

```
omni-dev drive sheets text-to-columns <ID> [--sheet NAME] --source <A1> \
  --delimiter comma|semicolon|period|space|auto|custom [--custom-delimiter TEXT] \
  [--dry-run] [--lease TOKEN] [-o table|json|yaml]
```

- Verb `text-to-columns` (15 chars, within #1830's 27 limit). `--source` matches the API field and `auto-fill`'s form B; `--delimiter` is a clap `value_enum` mirroring the API rather than a bare literal, so `--delimiter comma` can never be mistaken for the text `comma`. `--custom-delimiter` `requires`/is `required_if_eq` `custom` and is refused with any other type (clap-level, plus an engine check so the JSON/MCP path cannot bypass it — the pattern `find-replace` uses).
- `--source` must be **exactly one column wide**; rows may be bounded (`A2:A100`) or the whole column (`A:A`, the spreadsheet idiom for this operation). A multi-column, row-only or whole-sheet reference is `RefusedInvalidRange` with the "must span exactly one column" wording. Whole-column is accepted because `values.get` tolerates open rows and the grid-edge caveat only concerns the *column* axis; for A1 rendering and read offsets an open row bound is treated as row 0 / the grid `rowCount`. This is the one judgment call in the plan — if a bounded-only rule (`auto-fill`/`sort-range`'s) is preferred, it is a two-line change.

### Preview algorithm (§6, one bounded read beyond the light `spreadsheets.get`)

1. `spreadsheets.get` → `sheetId` + grid extent (every `GridRange` verb already does this).
2. `values.get` of the **source column** (formatted values, as `auto-fill` reads). For each row compute the piece count under the chosen delimiter with a naive `str::split` (no quote handling, no consecutive-delimiter collapsing); **width W = max pieces**. For `auto`, W = max over the four fixed delimiters. Only a count leaves this step — the pieces are dropped immediately and never stored on the outcome.
3. **Spill span** = the W−1 columns to the right of the source, over the source rows (the source column itself is rewritten with piece 1, but its content is the input, not a casualty, so it is excluded from the overwritten list and the output says so). W ≤ 1 ⇒ "no row splits under this delimiter; the request would write nothing beyond the source" — still sendable, since the server's rule may differ.
4. `values.get` of the spill span, **clamped to the grid** via the existing `grid_range::clamp_to_sheet` (the `paste.rs` helper; `auto_fill.rs` carries a private duplicate `clamp_to_grid`) — so a spill past `columnCount` sets the `past_grid_extent` caveat instead of failing the read and pre-empting §5's "left to the server". Non-blank cells → `overwritten_cells`, **always** flagged `overwritten_cells_upper_bound: true` — the naive split can only over-count (quoted delimiters, collapsed spaces), and a server that writes *fewer* columns overwrites a subset of the span; this direction is one of the live items below.
5. Summary is **tense-neutral** (reused verbatim as the log's `fields_changed`): `split 'Q1'!A2:A100 on comma into up to 4 column(s), spill 'Q1'!B2:D100`, followed by `up to N non-blank cell(s) would be/were overwritten: B3, C3, …`, the `auto` note (`delimiter is detected by Sheets`) when applicable, and the `PAST_GRID_EXTENT` caveat pair in the matching tense.
